description: Count execution records per order type, so each fill counts separately, and then compute shares and the above-average summary from those counts.

c.request: Link each order execution to its order (where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`), and ignore executions without a matching order. Find how many executed orders each order type (`ordertune`) has, with a missing order type treated as its own group. Then work out each type's share of the total as a fraction. Looking only at the order types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return a single unrounded row with: the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that overall average share. Count execution records per order type, so each fill counts separately, and then compute shares and the above-average summary from those counts.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS ordertune, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), shares AS (SELECT ordertune, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM counts) AS share FROM counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - av.a) AS avg_excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share av WHERE s.share > av.a

a.request: Link each order execution to its order (where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`), and drop any execution without a matching order. Count execution records per order type (`ordertune`); an order with several executions counts once per execution, and a missing order type forms its own group. Then work out each type's share of the total count as a fraction. Looking only at the order types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return a single unrounded row with: the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that overall average share.
a.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS ot, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT ot, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

b.request: Inner join orderexecutions to orders on recordvault = ordersmark, count each execution record (each fill counted separately) per ordertune with NULL ordertune as its own group, compute each type's share as its count divided by the total count across all types, then among types whose share is strictly greater than the average share across all types, return one unrounded row with the sum of their counts, the average of their shares, and the average of (their share minus the overall average share)
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS t, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orderexecutions e INNER JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT t, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT t, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_share_diff FROM a WHERE share > avg_share
